AC Repair in Conroe, TX, for a City That Keeps Adding Rooftops

Conroe has added tens of thousands of residents since 2010, so many of its air conditioners are young and many of its owners are new to Texas summers. Ring the free line at any hour and get passed to a locally owned HVAC business working in Conroe.

Call (832) 662-4107 Who powers your home
  1. Home

A search for AC repair in Conroe, TX, can come from a family in a subdivision finished last year or from someone opening up a lake house after a month away. Conroe is growing fast, part of it runs on a utility most of greater Houston never deals with, and its summers are as long and humid as anywhere in the region. What follows covers those Conroe quirks and what a call to the line looks like.

Houston Air & Heating does no HVAC work itself. Phone (832) 662-4107, tell the automated assistant the symptom and your part of Conroe, and the call is handed to a heating and cooling business that is owned locally and works in town. It sends the technician, sets the price for the job and collects payment from you, not from the line.

Conroe: the county seat that keeps growing

Conroe is the seat of Montgomery County, with Lake Conroe just west of town and Interstate 45 running through it. The Census Bureau counted 56,207 people here in 2010 and 89,956 in 2020. Its estimate for July 2024 was 114,581, roughly 27 percent above the 2020 count in just over four years.

Growth like that means thousands of homes with fairly new equipment, often under builder or manufacturer warranties. If your system is only a few years old, find the paperwork before you call. The company you reach will want the install date, and a warranty can change who pays for a failed part, although labor is often billed separately.

Entergy Texas or CenterPoint: who delivers your power

Much of greater Houston has one wires company and a long list of retail providers. Conroe is different. Look at your bill to see which situation you are in.

If your bill says Entergy Texas

Entergy Texas is a regulated utility. Its Southeast Texas service area was never opened to retail competition, so you buy electricity from Entergy itself and report outages to Entergy. Entergy has done reliability upgrades in Conroe and restored service here after storms.

If your bill names a retail provider

You are likely in CenterPoint's delivery area. CenterPoint keeps up the poles and lines and fixes outages; the bill itself comes from whichever retailer you signed with. You can switch retail providers; you cannot switch wires companies.

Storm outages and what to do when power returns

Severe storms reach Conroe as well as the coast. After storms in late May 2025, Entergy Texas reported a peak of 31,760 customers without power across its Southeast Texas system early on May 27, and by the next afternoon most of the remaining outages were in the Conroe area. When the power comes back after a long outage, a few steps protect your system:

  1. Wait a few minutes before asking the AC to run, so the power has a chance to settle.
  2. Check the breaker for the outdoor unit and give a tripped one a single reset, and if it flips off a second time, stop.
  3. Look outside for branches or debris against the condenser and pull them clear with the system off.
  4. Call if it will not cool after an hour or two of running, or if you hear grinding, buzzing or clicking without the fan starting.

Lake Conroe homes that sit empty

Plenty of houses around the lake are weekend places or second homes. In a Gulf Coast summer, shutting the air conditioner off while you are away lets the humidity inside climb, because the system is also the main thing drying the air. Before you leave for a stretch, set the thermostat higher rather than off, replace a dirty filter, and look at the condensate line where it drains outside to make sure it is not plugged. A thermostat that alerts your phone when the indoor temperature climbs can warn you before a breakdown turns into a moldy closet.

Entergy Texas efficiency programs

If Entergy delivers your power, ask about its energy efficiency offers before you pay for maintenance or upgrades. Entergy Texas has held CoolSaver events in some of the communities it serves, where its efficiency team worked with local contractors to give qualifying customers A/C tune-ups at no cost, and some homes also received weatherization such as air sealing, attic insulation and duct sealing. Locations, programs and eligibility change, so confirm the current terms with Entergy and ask the HVAC company whether it takes part.

Before you approve work in Conroe

  • Ask about permits. Conroe has its own city government. Find out from the contractor if the job calls for a City of Conroe permit and inspection, and have it written on the quote. If your Conroe address is outside city limits, ask what applies there instead.
  • Ask about the warranty. For a newer home, ask whether the part is covered and what labor will cost.
  • Ask for the license number. A Texas ACR contractor license shows up on the TDLR search within seconds.

With a gas furnace, leaks belong to the gas utility printed on your monthly statement. Any gas odor means walking outside before you dial that utility's emergency number or 911. A beeping carbon monoxide detector means the whole household leaves the house first, then calls 911.

Verify the license before work begins. Texas requires anyone contracting to do air conditioning, refrigeration or heating work to hold an Air Conditioning and Refrigeration (ACR) Contractor license from the Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation (TDLR). Ask the company for its ACR license number, then confirm it on the TDLR license search (opens in a new tab). The line does not check this for you.

Common questions

Is Conroe electricity Entergy or CenterPoint?

Both companies serve the Conroe area, so it depends on your address. Entergy Texas has announced reliability work and storm restoration in Conroe, and retail comparison sites list CenterPoint in the area too. Your electric bill names the company that delivers your power. Either way, neither one repairs air conditioners.

Can I pick my electricity provider if Entergy serves my Conroe home?

No. Entergy Texas operates as a regulated utility, and its Southeast Texas area was never opened to retail competition, so you buy power directly from Entergy. Homes in CenterPoint's area choose a retail provider instead.

Should I turn the AC off at my Lake Conroe weekend house?

Turning it off completely in summer lets indoor humidity climb, because the air conditioner is also what pulls moisture out of the air. Many owners leave it running at a higher setting instead. Ask the HVAC company what setting and what humidity control make sense for a house that sits empty.

Does Entergy Texas offer free AC tune-ups in Conroe?

Not as a standing offer. Entergy Texas has run CoolSaver events in specific communities it serves, such as the Cleveland, Huntsville, Orange and Dayton areas, where qualifying customers received A/C tune-ups at no cost and some homes also got weatherization such as duct sealing and attic insulation. Entergy says it plans to bring these services to more communities, so check with Entergy Texas about Conroe before you count on one.

Who checks that a Conroe HVAC company is licensed?

You do, in about a minute. Request the Texas ACR contractor license number, then type it into TDLR's online license search. The line does not do this check for you.
